question: What is the exact number of Principles in the PRINCE2 7th Edition method?
explanation: PRINCE2 has exactly seven Principles. All of them are universal and mandatory.

question: Is a project that applies six of the seven principles managed using PRINCE2?
options: Yes, if the omitted principle does not affect the budget
No, because all seven principles are mandatory
Yes, if the project manager approves the omission
Only when the project is short and small
explanation: No. All seven principles must be applied. PINO (PRINCE in Name Only) is a label from outside the textbook.

question: Which TWO of the following are integrated elements of PRINCE2 7? Choose ONE pair of true statements. 1. People.  2. Practices.  3. Gantt charts.  4. Jira software.
explanation: The textbook identifies five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT one of the seven PRINCE2 Principles?
explanation: PRINCE2 is independent of specific programming and IT tools; using MS Project is not a Principle.

question: What does the concept of Sustainability, given greater emphasis in PRINCE2 7th Edition, define?
options: Focusing exclusively on the company’s maximum financial profit.
Relating the project to one, some or all of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals.
Guaranteeing that the source code will never need corrections.
explanation: In PRINCE2, sustainability may address one, some or all of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals, project-work impacts, whole-life product cost and resilience, or a project objective.

question:
Complete the following sentence:
The process in which the project is first assessed, before the project is initiated, to determine whether it is worth pursuing is [...] a project.
explanation: The Starting up a project (SU) process takes place before the project and checks whether it is worth proceeding to initiation.

question: Which TWO objectives belong to the seven performance targets used to control a project in PRINCE2 7? Choose ONE pair of true statements. 1. Time.  2. Sustainability.  3. Number of social media followers.  4. The project manager’s personal brand.
explanation: The seven performance targets are time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability.

question: Which statement correctly describes the project initiation documentation (PID)?
options: It is assembled during initiating a project
It is completed entirely during starting up a project
It contains only quality test results
explanation: The PID is assembled during initiating a project (IP), based on the Project Brief produced in SU. It is not completed entirely in SU and does not replace stage plans.

question: Which statement best describes the project context as an integrated element of PRINCE2?
options: It is the activity list for the seven processes
It concerns only the project team’s needs
It should be understood by stakeholders so the method can be applied appropriately
It defines only the schedule structure
explanation: The project context affects how people apply the principles, practices and processes and how the method is tailored.

question: Which definition best describes a project?
options: A permanent function that maintains operations
A collection of unrelated tasks with no business owner
Any work performed by a team
A temporary organization delivering products under an agreed business case
explanation: A project is temporary, delivers agreed products and operates within an agreed business justification.

question: What best describes project management?
options: The project manager personally creating every product
Coordinating the project and motivating people to achieve its objectives
Operating the product after the project
explanation: Project management coordinates all aspects and people’s work so that the project objectives can be achieved.

question: Which TWO statements describe typical project characteristics? 1. It is temporary. 2. It always has the same team. 3. It introduces change. 4. It is less risky than BAU.
explanation: Temporary organization and change are typical characteristics. Teams and contexts vary, and uncertainty usually makes projects riskier than BAU.

question: Which project characteristic distinguishes it from business as usual (BAU)?
options: A project always uses a familiar team
Every project differs from previous projects in some way
explanation: Uniqueness may arise from the team, customer, supplier, product, location or timeframe.

question: Which TWO are among the seven project performance targets? 1. Scope. 2. Benefits. 3. Number of meetings. 4. Executive popularity.
explanation: The seven targets are time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability.

question: Complete the sentence. In a [...] delivery method, work passes through broadly successive phases and the product is may be delivered during the work or at the end.
explanation: A linear-sequential approach organizes development in broadly successive phases; the product may be delivered during the work or at the end.

question: What characterizes an iterative-incremental delivery method?
options: The product evolves through repeated cycles and successive increments
The whole product appears only after one sequence of phases
explanation: Iterations enable learning and refinement, while increments progressively extend a usable product.

question: When is a hybrid delivery method most appropriate?
options: When different parts of the project require a combination of linear and iterative approaches
When the project has no products
explanation: A hybrid consciously combines delivery methods to suit different products or workstreams.

question: Which TWO statements concern the project context? 1. Contractual arrangements belong to commercial context. 2. Culture and policies belong to organizational context. 3. Context does not affect tailoring. 4. Scale is identical for every organization.
explanation: Trading relationships shape commercial context, while structures, culture and policies shape organizational context. Both affect tailoring.

question: How does PRINCE2 7 treat sustainability?
options: Only as an emissions measurement after closure
As a replacement for the business case
As a cross-cutting concern embedded throughout the method
explanation: Sustainability requirements may relate to the relevant UN Sustainable Development Goals and should be embedded in project management.

question: What does scale mean in the project context?
options: A fixed category shared by every organization
The project's relative size and significance for its organization
Only a system’s technical ability to support more users
The number of pages in the documentation
explanation: Project scale is relative to the organization and is not the same as a product's technical scalability.

question: Which TWO are PRINCE2 features or benefits? 1. Common language and concepts. 2. Universal application. 3. Mandatory software. 4. Identical documentation for every project.
explanation: PRINCE2 provides common language and is universal yet flexible. It does not prescribe one tool or identical documentation.

question: How does PRINCE2 help increase organizational maturity?
options: It requires repeating the same mistakes
It promotes learning from experience and continual improvement
It removes the need for reviews
explanation: Systematic use of lessons and improvement strengthens the organization’s ability to manage projects successfully.

question: What does it mean that PRINCE2 is part of an integrated suite of methods?
options: It applies only to IT projects
It can work with approaches for programme, portfolio and risk management
It can be used only with one software tool
It replaces every other management discipline
explanation: PRINCE2 can operate alongside complementary PeopleCert approaches for programmes, portfolios and risk.

question: Which management product provides the agreed reference for directing and managing the project after initiation?
explanation: The PID is assembled during initiating a project and brings together the agreed basis for directing and managing it.
